description: baseline: 2.4 tok/s, 162 tests pass, temp>0 untested (demo hardcodes temp=0)
remove ~130 lines diagnostics from mlx-worker.ts (code quality, equal perf)
fix temp>0: pure Rust categorical sampling avoids WASM heap exhaustion
perf: batch size 64→512, setPipeline/setBindGroup dedup (+12%)
fuse setPipeline+setBindGroup+dispatch into single RPC (+46%)
buffer size caching: no improvement, high variance in benchmark
reuse compute pass across dispatches, skip begin/end/release RPCs (+22%)
skip bind group/layout/shader release RPCs (+8%)
skip buffer destroy RPC (was already no-op on gpu-worker)
cache buffer sizes with plain object, skip ~71K RPCs (+31%)
optimize rpcCall hot path, remove debug tracking
C++ kernel improvements: conv1d, bf16 offset fix, 159/163 tests (+8% tok/s, -27% TTFT)
FUSED_SUBMIT: collapse 6 RPCs→1 per encoder submit (pass_end+finish+submit+3 releases). Needs Chrome benchmark.
CREATE_BUFFER_FROM_DATA: fuse createBuffer+writeBuffer into 1 RPC. Uniform buffers 3→1 RPCs/dispatch. Playwright: 5.0→5.3 tok/s (+6%).
FUSED_FULL_DISPATCH: inline bind group creation in dispatch RPC. Eliminates ~100 CREATE_BIND_GROUP RPCs/token. Playwright: 5.3→6.6 tok/s (+25%). TTFT 626ms.
FUSED_DISPATCH_WITH_UNIFORM: inline writeBuffer in dispatch RPC. 2→1 RPCs per dispatch after warmup. Playwright: 6.6→10.1 tok/s (+53%). TTFT 435ms.
FUSED_COPY_BUFFER: end pass + copy + begin pass in 1 RPC. No perf gain (copies rare in decode). Correctness improvement only.
Optimize rpcCall hot path: Uint32Array direct indexing + explicit params (no array alloc). ~3% improvement.
gpu-worker Uint32Array reads: replace DataView with cmdU32 for arg readers, result setters, entry reads in FUSED_FULL_DISPATCH/FUSED_DISPATCH_WITH_UNIFORM. Playwright: 10.4→10.8 tok/s.
SPINLOCK: replaced Atomics.wait with busy-wait loop in rpcCall. Starves gpu-worker of CPU time in browser thread scheduling → massive regression 10.4→5.5 tok/s. Reverted.

FAST-PATH DISPATCH: inline hot-path handlers (FUSED_FULL_DISPATCH, FUSED_DISPATCH_WITH_UNIFORM) in command loop, bypassing async processCommand + 13 closure allocs + switch dispatch + flushCallbacks. Playwright: 10.8→13.4 tok/s (+24%), TTFT 443→393ms (-11%).

ADAPTIVE SPIN: after dispatch RPCs, gpu-worker spins 2000 iterations checking for next PENDING before falling back to Atomics.waitAsync. Avoids V8 event loop scheduling overhead (~50-100μs) for back-to-back dispatches. Playwright: 13.4→17.5 tok/s (+31%), TTFT 393→316ms (-20%).

RAW SPIN READ: replaced Atomics.load with raw cmdView[STATUS_INDEX] in spin loop. V8 JIT hoists the read out of the loop, returning stale cached values → spin never catches PENDING → massive regression 17.5→12.7 tok/s. Must use Atomics.load. Reverted.

Fused SDPA vector kernel: Q·K^T → softmax → ·V in single WGSL dispatch for Tq=1 decode path. Two-phase algorithm (max/sum then weighted V accumulation), workgroup=128, subgroup reductions when available. Dispatches B*H workgroups, each thread owns one output lane via if (tid < D). Pipeline cache keyed on (dtype, D, has_mask, has_subgroups). Gated by use_fallback: tq==1, d∈{64,96,128}, f32/bf16, row-contiguous, no training/logsumexp. Playwright: 17.5→20 tok/s (+14.3%), 162/163 tests pass, output coherent, temp>0 works.

Single-pass chunked SDPA: eliminate Phase A-2 (redundant K traversal) and Phase B score recomputation by caching exp-weights in shared_red per chunk. Each chunk: (1) all threads compute weight_l and thread_sum, (2) threads tid<D accumulate V-weighted contributions using cached weights. Final sum reduction + normalization. K reads per workgroup: ~L·D² → ~2·L·D (128x reduction for D=128). 6-sample bimodal distribution: cold runs 19.3,20.6 (mean 19.95) ~= baseline 20; warm runs 23.6-24.8 (mean 24.1) — TTFT pattern 491→296 confirms system-level warmup noise unrelated to kernel change (SDPA gated to Tq=1, doesn't touch prompt phase). Neutral on cold-to-cold comparison; kept for architectural simplicity and to unblock chunk-size/V-tiling optimizations. Tests 162/163, coherent, temp>0 works.

Pipeline warmup at model load: run a 2-token dummy inference (maxNewTokens:2) immediately after Qwen35Model.loadFromGpuBuffers() to force WebGPU pipeline compilation for all kernels in the decode hot path. Warmup wraps in try/catch so failures don't block model readiness. Playwright 5 samples: decode mean 25.7 tok/s (20→25.7, +28.5%), TTFT mean 219ms (461→219ms, -52%). Stddev drops from ~25% to ~1.4% because cold-start pipeline compilation no longer contaminates the measurement — double win: real perf improvement AND much cleaner benchmark methodology. Tests 162/163.

Split-K GEMV kernel: rewrite make_gemv_kernel from 'one thread per output element' to 'one workgroup per output element, 256 threads cooperatively reduce K'. Two wins: (1) Coalesced B reads in the common b_transposed case — all 256 threads share col and iterate k, reading 256 adjacent K elements per iteration. The naive kernel had adjacent threads striding by ldb (=K), fully uncoalesced. (2) ~100x more active threads: N=3072 → 3072 wg × 256 threads = 786k threads vs old 12 wg × 256 = 3k. Workgroup reduction uses emit_subgroup_reduction when has_subgroups (pipeline key _sg suffix), fallback to emit_unrolled_reduction. Dispatch uses 2D fanout with GRID_X=65535 so lm_head (vocab ≈ 151k) fits. Playwright 5 samples: mean 28.1 ± 1.3 tok/s vs 25.7 baseline (+9.3%, +40.5% over original 20). TTFT stable ~220ms. 162/163 tests, coherent, temp>0 works.

notes: Amortize A-vector loads across 4 output columns. New make_gemv_multi_col_kernel with wg=128, 4 accumulators, 4 parallel reductions. Dispatcher picks multi-col when kind==GEMV && N>=16. Reduces memory traffic from 2NK to 5NK/4 (-37.5%) for lm_head/down_proj/gate_up_proj.

experiment: parameterize multi-col GEMV + add COLS_PER_WG=8 variant for N >= 512
notes: Parameterize make_gemv_multi_col_kernel on cols_per_wg (emits via C++ for loops). Add kMultiCol8Threshold=512: gate/up (N=4864), down (N=896), lm_head (N=151936), q/o_proj (N=896) use 8-col; k/v_proj (N=128) stays 4-col. Memory traffic 1.25K→1.125K per col (-10%). 8-col thresh picked so workgroup count stays healthy (lowest-N case is q_proj at 112 wgs). Marginal +2.2% is within noise but consistent (6/7 samples above old mean). Pipeline prefix split gemv_mc4_/gemv_mc8_ avoids cache collisions. Comment drift cleaned up in follow-up commit 3ce5bb47. Excluded 1 cold-start outlier (27.3 tok/s, TTFT=446) caused by vite dev-server warmup.

Added 3rd multi-col branch at N>=32768 (targets lm_head N=151936). Memory traffic per col: 17K/16 vs 9K/8 (~5.6% reduction for mc16). Shared memory cost 16*128*4=8KB fits. 8 samples: 30.6,26.2,29.5,30.0,30.5,28.7,28.6,30.2. Mean 29.29, excl cold 29.73 (vs baseline 30.57). No measurable improvement, slight regression within noise. Probable causes: (1) register pressure from 16 accumulators per thread increases occupancy limit, (2) pipeline compile cost added to warmup for one-off dispatch, (3) lm_head bandwidth already saturated by mc8, diminishing returns. Reverted matmul.cpp; restored baseline bench shows 30.4-35.4 range confirming noise level. Discarded: mc16 not worth the added shader variant.

Doubled multi-col GEMV workgroup size from 128 to 256 to match the single-col kernel and halve per-thread K-loop iterations. Updated shared array size (128→256), @workgroup_size attr, subgroup reduction tree to match 8 subgroups (8→4→2→1 instead of 4→2→1), and non-SG reduction start stride (64→128). 6 samples: 29.3,30.6,30.2,31.3,30.4,31.0 = mean 30.47 (vs baseline 30.57). Primary metric neutral (within noise). TTFT slightly better at 199.5ms vs ~210ms (-5%, noise-adjacent). Tests 162/163, output coherent, temp>0 works — kernel correct. Hypothesis why no speedup: for K=896 in Qwen3.5, 128 threads already cover K in 7 iterations — latency-hidden loop is short enough that 4 iterations with more threads doesn't help. Dispatch overhead per workgroup also scales inversely, canceling gains. Discarded: no primary-metric improvement despite consistency with single-col.

hypothesis: Qwen3.5 weight shapes all have N divisible by cols_per_wg (8); has1..hasN-1 bounds guards in K-loop are pure overhead. Add n_aligned fast path that skips these guards.

changes.mlx/backend/webgpu/matmul.cpp: Added bool n_aligned parameter to make_gemv_multi_col_kernel. When N % cols_per_wg == 0, skip emission of has1..hasN-1 declarations, skip if(hasI) guards on K-loop FMAs, skip guards on output stores. dispatch_matmul computes n_aligned and appends _al suffix to pipeline cache key.

notes: Consistent +2.3% across 5 samples, zero variance. TTFT also improved ~8%. Guards were loop-invariant but still produced predicated branches that cost latency. Removing them unblocks K-loop FMA chain.

hypothesis: Explicit let bv0..bv7 declarations before FMAs will expose the loads as an independent batch for parallel issue, hiding memory latency.

changes.mlx/backend/webgpu/matmul.cpp: In n_aligned fast path, emit let bvI = f32(b[...]) for all i first, then emit acc_i += a_val * bv_i for all i. Both !b_transposed and b_transposed branches.

notes: Slower and more variable. The compiler already schedules loads optimally; forcing explicit temporaries increases register pressure without benefit. Reverted.

hypothesis: Replace the 2-stage cross-subgroup tree reduction with a single subgroupAdd inside sg_id==0 block to save 1 barrier per reduction.

changes.mlx/backend/webgpu/matmul.cpp: In multi-col GEMV reduction, replaced tid<2 and tid<1 stride reductions with an if (sg_id == 0u) { subgroupAdd(lane<4 ? shared[lane] : 0) } block.

notes: WGSL subgroup ops require workgroup-uniform control flow, not subgroup-uniform. Calling subgroupAdd inside 'if (sg_id == 0u)' is undefined behavior. Output was incoherent AND slower. Reverted.

trigger: External reviewer feedback: bf16 stored as f32 on GPU doubles read bandwidth for memory-bound GEMV
proposed_stages: Side table for packed bf16 weight buffers on wgpu::device()
matmul.cpp: new GEMV variant reading array<u32> and unpacking bf16 via bitcast
Extend to SDPA and vocab logits reductions
rationale: Multi-file refactor spanning TS/Rust FFI/C++; requires design review of loadFromGpuBuffers API change. Continuing autoresearch with smaller experiments while tracked as high-ROI follow-up.

hypothesis: Read B as array<vec4<f32>> in n_aligned !b_transposed path to halve memory transactions (16-byte coalesced loads).

changes.mlx/backend/webgpu/matmul.cpp: Added b_vec4 param to make_gemv_multi_col_kernel; emits @binding(1) var<storage, read> b: array<vec4<f32>> when active; K-loop reads let bvec_v = b[b_row_v4 + v] and unpacks .x/.y/.z/.w into cols_per_wg/4 accumulators. dispatch_matmul checks ldb%4, batch_stride_b%4, b_elem_offset%4.

notes: The code gated on !b_transposed, but Qwen3.5 linear layers (lm_head, q/k/v/o_proj, gate/up/down_proj) all go through check_transpose and land on the b_transposed path where 4 output cols are stored non-contiguously (strided by ldb). vec4<f32> reads would only help if 4 cols were adjacent in memory. The +2.3% measured on first pass was within benchmark noise — a clean-baseline resample after revert shows the same 32.0-32.9 mean. Reverted matmul.cpp to run 32 state. Lesson: always verify which branch of a kernel actually fires for production shapes before trusting a marginal tok/s delta. To capture the 16-byte coalesced load benefit on the b_transposed side we'd need a different reshape: read A as vec4 (stride-K contiguous), which is the next experiment candidate but was not pursued in this session.

status: User satisfied with current perf (≈32 tok/s, TTFT ≈196ms, 162/163 tests, coherent output, temp>0 works). Stopping autoresearch loop.
